content.title: Toggle the benchmark display off and back on from Customize
content.intent: Prove the performance chart removes the benchmark line and related legend when Benchmark is disabled and restores them when re-enabled.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: state / flow + equivalence partitioning. This is an outcome-changing toggle family, so it is its own scenario rather than a parameter on another chart-option path. Risk strength judged as 2 because only user-reach applied; no money, auth, or data-loss factors were evidenced.

content.title: Disable hover indicators from Customize and remove active hover marker behavior
content.intent: Prove disabling Hover Indicators prevents the performance chart from showing its active hover marker when the chart is hovered.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: state / flow + negative. Hover-marker absence is a distinct outcome from other chart options, so it stays separate. Risk strength judged as 2 because only user-reach applied; no money, auth, or data-loss factors were evidenced.

content.title: Disable chart grid from Customize and remove performance chart grid lines

content.technique_notes: Techniques: state / flow + equivalence partitioning. Grid visibility is a separate chart-option outcome, so it is not collapsed into Benchmark or Hover Indicators. Risk strength judged as 2 because only user-reach applied; no money, auth, or data-loss factors were evidenced.

content.title: Toggle a standard dashboard section off and back on from Customize
content.intent: Prove a standard card section can be hidden, the surrounding layout closes the gap, and the section returns when re-enabled.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: equivalence partitioning over section-layout classes + state / flow. I used Allocation as the representative standard card section because the grid defines it as a 4-column peer beside Performance, making local reflow observable. Risk strength judged as 2 because only user-reach applied; no money, auth, or data-loss factors were evidenced.

content.technique_notes: Techniques: equivalence partitioning over section-layout classes + state / flow. content.technique_notes: Techniques: equivalence partitioning. content.title: Use keyboard controls to operate the Customize drawer options
content.intent: Prove the customize drawer controls remain operable with keyboard navigation and selection, with visible focus and no hover-only dependency.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: a11y + state / flow. The accessibility requirements and keyboard requirements apply to all functionality and explicitly require keyboard operation, visible focus, and non-hover-exclusive interaction, so Customize controls need a dedicated keyboard path. Risk strength judged as 2 because only user-reach applied; no money, auth, or data-loss factors were evidenced.
